title: A retrospective analysis of risk factors, treatments and outcomes in severe peripartum haemorrhage at St. Joseph Hospital from 2010 to 2020.
summary: Postpartum haemorrhage is one of the most common and dangerous complications during childbirth. It can lead to serious health problems and even death. This study looks at all cases at St. Joseph Hospital Berlin between 2010 and 2020 where women experienced severe bleeding after birth that required a blood transfusion. Researchers aim to find out which factors increase the risk of such bleeding, how the bleeding was treated, and what outcomes were achieved for mother and child. The data will be taken from existing medical records and analysed anonymously.

interventions.name:
Retrospective analysis of all patients treated at St. Joseph Hospital Berlin between 2010 and 2020 for severe peripartum haemorrhage who received at least one transfusion of packed red blood cells during delivery.
Clinical parameters, risk factors, treatment measures and outcomes will be extracted

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Admission under the Department of Obstetrics or Gynaecology.
Delivery occurred during the hospital stay.
Transfusion of at least one unit of packed red blood cells directly related to delivery.
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or incomplete transfusion documentation in the patient record.
No mention of postpartum or obstetric haemorrhage in discharge summary, operation report, transfusion documentation or clinical notes.
No plausible temporal or clinical relationship between birth and transfusion.
Transfusion given for a reason other than haemorrhage (e.g., chronic anaemia or other underlying condition).
Patients under 18 years of age.
